children: The Indian rupee opened 2 paise stronger at 95.57 against the US dollar on Wednesday (September 23), compared with its previous close of 95.59, as traders continued to track crude oil prices and developments around the US-Iran conflict.

Oil prices remained a key factor for Indian financial markets, with Brent crude futures hovering near two-week lows at around $99.22 a barrel amid hopes that diplomatic efforts at the United Nations General Assembly could help resolve the conflict.

For India, movements in crude oil prices are closely watched because the country imports a large share of its crude oil requirement. Higher oil prices can increase the country's import bill and demand for dollars, potentially putting pressure on the rupee. Conversely, a moderation in crude prices can reduce pressure on the import bill.

The rupee's opening value of 95.57 per US dollar means it costs ₹95.57 to buy one US dollar in the foreign exchange market. Since it had closed at ₹95.59, the currency strengthened by 2 paise, or ₹0.02, against the dollar.
Such a small daily movement does not by itself indicate a significant change in the rupee's broader trend. Traders are also watching oil prices, foreign fund flows and developments in global markets.
Analysts at MUFG said oil prices had moderated somewhat from their highs but cautioned that the outlook remained unclear given uncertainty over a possible resolution to the conflict.

Foreign portfolio investors have remained a source of pressure on Indian equities. Overseas investors sold Indian shares worth $1.81 billion in September so far, taking their year-to-date outflows to $25.87 billion, according to stock depository data.

Weak capital flows, along with pressure from India's elevated energy import bill, have weighed on the rupee. The impact has been partly absorbed by intervention from the Reserve Bank of India, according to traders.

India's foreign exchange reserves have also risen to a record level after the central bank accumulated foreign currency through one-off policy measures aimed at attracting capital inflows, providing an additional buffer for the currency.

title: Rupee edges higher to 95.57 against dollar as crude prices ease
